No per-sample or per-subject identifiers are provided in the accessible text; subject_id and sample_id fields could not be populated, and granularity was set to subgroup_level (country x age-band) rather than sample_level.
study_name was not explicitly stated in the paper text; left as not_reported rather than inferring a convention-based ID.

Age-group enum assignment for 'children' subgroups (Ghana 0-15 yrs, Tanzania 0-18 yrs) is approximate since these ranges span multiple schema-defined age bins (Infant/Child/Adolescent); assigned based on mean age.

Family role and lifestyle classification for Ethiopia cohort limited to what was directly stated (mothers/infants); no explicit lifestyle description provided beyond geographic/administrative location.
Sex distribution for Ghana and Tanzania adult subgroups reported as percentages (mixed-sex) and could not be reduced to a single enum value without fabrication.

This paper is primarily a microbial genomics/population-genetics study (Prevotella copri); most clinical/host metadata fields in the schema (disease response, treatment, neonatal details, HLA, zygosity, etc.) are not reported for the study's own cohorts.

Age data are reported as subgroup-level aggregates (mean, SD, range) for adult/child/infant groups within each country (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania), not as per-participant values; treated as subgroup_level granularity.

Disease status 'Healthy' pertains to the newly sequenced Ghana/Ethiopia/Tanzania cohorts only; the paper separately analyzes previously published disease cohorts (CRC, T2D, hypertension, cirrhosis, IBD) via meta-analysis of public metagenomes, but no participant-level disease metadata for those external cohorts is given in this text.
Sex distribution and family/twin structure data exist in the text but were not requested by schema fields other than zygosity (which is not reported).
